explanation: The Western 'all good' meaning of the OK sign doesn't reliably carry over to the Gulf: general references on obscene gestures note it carries vulgar or offensive connotations in parts of the Middle East, and at least one UAE-focused etiquette source describes it locally as evoking the 'evil eye' rather than approval. Because interpretations vary by generation and audience, and solid country-specific evidence is thin, treat it as genuinely unpredictable rather than safe.
local_tip: Use a verbal 'great' or a simple nod of approval instead of the OK sign.

also_check.note: The gesture is considered a serious obscene insult.
It commonly signals 'money' or 'OK', though context still matters in very formal settings.
